problem: Navigation instruction generation (VL-GEN) relies on resource-intensive sequences of photo-realistic panoramic images, which contain many irrelevant details and force the model to do object recognition and instruction generation jointly.
motivation: Humans easily understand navigation from top-down maps, and robots can obtain semantic maps via semantic SLAM. Separating environment interpretation from spatial reasoning would give a lightweight, human-interpretable representation, so the paper asks whether a single top-down semantic map can serve as the main input for VL-GEN.
key_idea: Frame navigation instruction generation as image captioning over a single top-down semantic map with the path drawn on it, optionally augmented with region names, actions, panoramas and a landmark prompt, using a BLIP-base model.
insight: A single semantic map already gives SPICE on par with panorama-based Speaker-Follower and EnvDrop, and adding region+action text with a prompt gives a statistically significant gain (17.84 vs 16.19 unseen, p<=0.01). Error analysis shows the map-only model mostly hallucinates, especially left/right actions. Region/action inputs and prompting reduce hallucinations (10 down to 6), while contrastive loss brings redundancy and linguistic errors and does not help.
method: Task formulation: image captioning; input is a top-down semantic map M_s (colour-coded object bounding boxes, path drawn as connected points) and the output is the instruction D_P.

Data extraction: semantic maps, region names and heuristic actions (left/right/straight/stop, 20° threshold) extracted from Habitat/Matterport3D for R2R paths; 7 object types filtered out; one map per floor; map padded to 1024x1024 and masked to a 40-pixel neighbourhood of the path.
Map encoder: the BLIP ViT image encoder (patch 16) on the semantic map resized with nearest sampling.
Region + action encoder: region-name embeddings (BLIP text encoder, mean-pooled) added to action embeddings per navigation point, then a 3-layer LSTM over the path.
Panorama encoder: frozen BLIP image encoder plus a 2-layer MLP; panorama embeddings are mean-pooled over the path; all embeddings are summed as decoder input.
Contrastive auxiliary loss: CLIP-style loss between the input embedding and the instruction embedding, weighted 0.1.

Prompt: a template describing the nearby objects and region at the start point (e.g. 'Starting from the dark yellow point near sofa cushion in the living room region'), used in training and fed to the decoder at inference.

setting.backbone: BLIP-base image captioning model (fine-tuned) with LSTM for region/action inputs
setting.model_size: BLIP-base (~224M parameters, not stated in the paper)
setting.training_data: R2R train split (10,623 semantic-map paths with human instructions), extended with semantic maps, regions, actions and panoramas
setting.observation: top-down semantic map (single RGB image) with the path, plus optional region names, actions and panoramic RGB
setting.action_space: not applicable (text generation; heuristic discrete actions left/right/straight/stop are inputs)
setting.simulator: Habitat (semantic maps) and Matterport3D simulator (panoramas), based on R2R
setting.privileged: GT semantic map, region and action annotations from the simulator (in a real robot they would come from semantic SLAM)

numbers.evidence: Table 1: TD+Reg+Act, P checked: 17.84** unseen, human 4.29 (2)

numbers_note: Instruction generation benchmark (SPICE, human score 0-10), not a navigation benchmark; human scores are on 15 unseen paths rated by 5 evaluators.
results: Semantic-map-based variants reach SPICE up to 17.84 (unseen) / 22.14 (seen), on par with or above Speaker-Follower (17.0/18.7) and EnvDrop (18.1/20.2) reported for panorama-based models. Adding regions, actions and prompts significantly improves over the map-only baseline (16.19), and the human rating rises from 3.42 to 4.36 with panoramas. Absolute performance is still low.
limitations: The single-layer semantic map lacks region names and object properties (colour, material, shape, mentioned in about a third of instructions), so they must be supplied separately.
Semantic maps, regions and actions are taken from the simulator, and no real-robot semantic SLAM is used.
Small human evaluation (5 raters, 15 paths); absolute quality is low, with frequent hallucination of actions and regions.
